sanskrit: sa śabdo bharataśreṣṭha vyāpya sarvā diśo daśa pratisasvāna tatraiva kurupāṇḍavayor bale
english: That sound, O best of the Bhāratas, spreading through all the ten directions, echoed back upon the very hosts of the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tāvakā rathinas tatra dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau saṃrambhaṃ paramaṃ prāptās tvaramāṇā mahārathāḥ
english: Beholding Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya there, your car-warriors, the great chariot-fighters, were seized with the utmost fury and hastened forward.

sanskrit: atha kṛṣṇau mahābhāgau tāvakā dṛśya daṃśitau abhyadravanta saṃkruddhās tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then your warriors, seeing the two illustrious Kṛṣṇas clad in their armor, rushed against them in wrath, and that was a wondrous thing to behold.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tāvakās tu samīkṣyaiva vṛṣṇyandhakakurūttamau prāg atvarañ jighāṃsantas tathaiva vijayaḥ parān
english: Saṃjaya said: But your men, the moment they caught sight of the foremost of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas and Kurus, pressed forward eager to slay them; and even so did Vijaya, eager to slay his foes.

sanskrit: suvarṇacitrair vaiyāghraiḥ svanavadbhir mahārathaiḥ dīpayanto diśaḥ sarvā jvaladbhir iva pāvakaiḥ
english: With their great chariots gleaming with gold and clothed in tiger-skins, resounding as they rolled, they lit up all the directions as though with blazing fires.

sanskrit: rukmapṛṣṭhaiś ca duṣprekṣyaiḥ kārmukaiḥ pṛthivīpate kūjadbhir atulān nādān roṣitair uragair iva
english: With their bows gold-backed and hard to gaze upon, O lord of the earth, twanging forth incomparable notes like enraged serpents,

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ karṇo vṛṣaseno jayadrathaḥ kṛpaś ca madrarājaś ca drauṇiś ca rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Bhūriśravas, Śala, Karṇa, Vṛṣasena, Jayadratha, Kṛpa, the king of the Madras, and the son of Droṇa, foremost of car-warriors —

sanskrit: te pibanta ivākāśam aśvair aṣṭau mahārathāḥ vyarājayan daśa diśo vaiyāghrair hemacandrakaiḥ
english: those eight great chariot-warriors, seeming as if to drink up the sky with their steeds, made the ten directions resplendent with their tiger-skin coverings adorned with golden orbs.

sanskrit: te daṃśitāḥ susaṃrabdhā rathair meghaughanisvanaiḥ samāvṛṇvan diśaḥ sarvāḥ pārthaṃ ca viśikhaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Armored and furious, with their chariots rumbling like masses of clouds, they covered all the directions, and Pārtha as well, with their sharp shafts.

sanskrit: kaulūtakā hayāś citrā vahantas tān mahārathān vyaśobhanta tadā śīghrā dīpayanto diśo daśa
english: The spirited horses of the Kulūta breed, dappled and swift, bearing those great car-warriors, shone forth then, lighting up the ten directions.

sanskrit: ājāneyair mahāvegair nānādeśasamutthitaiḥ pārvatīyair nadījaiś ca saindhavaiś ca hayottamaiḥ
english: With steeds of noble lineage and great speed, sprung from many lands — mountain-bred, river-born, and of the Sindhu country, the finest of horses —

sanskrit: kuruyodhavarā rājaṃs tava putraṃ parīpsavaḥ dhanaṃjayarathaṃ śīghraṃ sarvataḥ samupādravan
english: the foremost of the Kuru warriors, O king, longing to protect your son, swiftly assailed the chariot of Dhanaṃjaya from every side.

sanskrit: te pragṛhya mahāśaṅkhān dadhmuḥ puruṣasattamāḥ pūrayanto divaṃ rājan pṛthivīṃ ca sasāgarām
english: Those best of men, taking up their great conches, blew them, filling heaven, O king, and the earth with its seas.

sanskrit: tathaiva dadhmatuḥ śaṅkhau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau pravarau sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvaśaṅkhavarau bhuvi devadattaṃ ca kaunteyaḥ pāñcajanyaṃ ca keśavaḥ
english: In like manner Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya, the foremost of all beings, blew their two conches, the best of all conches on earth — the son of Kuntī his Devadatta, and Keśava his Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: śabdas tu devadattasya dhanaṃjayasamīritaḥ pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca diśaś caiva samāvṛṇot
english: The sound of Devadatta, sent forth by Dhanaṃjaya, filled the earth, the firmament, and all the directions.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāñcajanyo 'pi vāsudevasamīritaḥ sarvaśabdān atikramya pūrayām āsa rodasī
english: So too the Pāñcajanya, sounded by Vāsudeva, surpassing all other sounds, filled heaven and earth.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne dāruṇe nādasaṃkule bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajanane śūrāṇāṃ harṣavardhane
english: While that terrible tumult of clamor raged on, striking terror into the timid and swelling the joy of the brave,

sanskrit: pravāditāsu bherīṣu jharjhareṣv ānakeṣu ca mṛdaṅgeṣu ca rājendra vādyamāneṣv anekaśaḥ
english: while kettledrums, jharjharas, tabors, and tom-toms were beaten, O lord of kings, sounding forth in countless number,

sanskrit: mahārathasamākhyātā duryodhanahitaiṣiṇaḥ amṛṣyamāṇās taṃ śabdaṃ kruddhāḥ paramadhanvinaḥ nānādeśyā mahīpālāḥ svasainyaparirakṣiṇaḥ
english: those renowned as mighty car-warriors, the well-wishers of Duryodhana, unable to brook that sound, the wrathful and supreme bowmen, kings of many lands, guardians of their own troops,

sanskrit: amarṣitā mahāśaṅkhān dadhmur vīrā mahārathāḥ kṛte pratikariṣyantaḥ keśavasyārjunasya ca
english: those heroes, the great chariot-warriors, in their indignation blew their great conches, resolved to answer the deed of Keśava and Arjuna.

sanskrit: babhūva tava tat sainyaṃ śaṅkhaśabdasamīritam udvignarathanāgāśvam asvastham iva cābhibho
english: That army of yours, stirred by the blasts of the conches, with its chariots, elephants, and horses thrown into agitation, seemed, O lord, as though disquieted.

sanskrit: tat prayuktam ivākāśaṃ śūraiḥ śaṅkhanināditam babhūva bhṛśam udvignaṃ nirghātair iva nāditam
english: The sky, as it were, set ringing by the heroes with the blare of conches, became greatly troubled, as though resounding with thunderclaps.

sanskrit: sa śabdaḥ sumahān rājan diśaḥ sarvā vyanādayat trāsayām āsa tat sainyaṃ yugānta iva saṃbhṛtaḥ
english: That mighty sound, O king, made all the directions resound and terrified that army, gathering like the doom of the world's end.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano 'ṣṭau ca rājānas te mahārathāḥ jayadrathasya rakṣārthaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ paryavārayan
english: Then Duryodhana and those eight kings, the great car-warriors, surrounded the son of Pāṇḍu for the protection of Jayadratha.

sanskrit: tato drauṇis trisaptatyā vāsudevam atāḍayat arjunaṃ ca tribhir bhallair dhvajam aśvāṃś ca pañcabhiḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa struck Vāsudeva with seventy-three arrows, and Arjuna with three broad-headed shafts, his banner and his horses with five.

sanskrit: tam arjunaḥ pṛṣatkānāṃ śataiḥ ṣaḍbhir atāḍayat atyartham iva saṃkruddhaḥ pratividdhe janārdane
english: Arjuna, exceedingly enraged because Janārdana had been struck, smote him in turn with six hundred arrows.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ dvādaśabhir viddhvā vṛṣasenaṃ tribhis tathā śalyasya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ muṣṭau ciccheda vīryavān
english: Piercing Karṇa with twelve arrows and Vṛṣasena with three, the valiant one cut asunder, at the grip, the bow of Śalya together with its arrow.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā dhanur anyat tu śalyo vivyādha pāṇḍavam bhūriśravās tribhir bāṇair hemapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Taking up another bow, Śalya pierced the son of Pāṇḍu; and Bhūriśravas struck him with three arrows, gold-feathered and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: karṇo dvātriṃśatā caiva vṛṣasenaś ca pañcabhiḥ jayadrathas trisaptatyā kṛpaś ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ madrarājaś ca daśabhir vivyadhuḥ phalgunaṃ raṇe
english: Karṇa with thirty-two, Vṛṣasena with five, Jayadratha with seventy-three, Kṛpa with ten arrows, and the king of the Madras with ten — all pierced Phalguna in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarāṇāṃ ṣaṣṭyā tu drauṇiḥ pārtham avākirat vāsudevaṃ ca saptatyā punaḥ pārthaṃ ca pañcabhiḥ
english: Then the son of Droṇa covered Pārtha with sixty arrows, Vāsudeva with seventy, and Pārtha again with five.

sanskrit: prahasaṃs tu naravyāghraḥ śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ pratyavidhyat sa tān sarvān darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: But that tiger among men, of the white steeds and with Kṛṣṇa for his charioteer, laughing, pierced them all in return, displaying the swiftness of his hand.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ dvādaśabhir viddhvā vṛṣasenaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ śalyasya samare cāpaṃ muṣṭideśe nyakṛntata
english: Piercing Karṇa with twelve and Vṛṣasena with three arrows, he cut off Śalya's bow at the place of the grip in the fight.

sanskrit: saumadattiṃ tribhir viddhvā śalyaṃ ca daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ śitair agniśikhākārair drauṇiṃ vivyādha cāṣṭabhiḥ
english: Piercing the son of Somadatta with three arrows and Śalya with ten sharp shafts shaped like tongues of flame, he struck the son of Droṇa with eight.

sanskrit: gautamaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā śaindhavaṃ ca śatena ha punar drauṇiṃ ca saptatyā śarāṇāṃ so 'bhyatāḍayat
english: He smote Gautama with twenty-five, the ruler of the Sindhus with a hundred, and the son of Droṇa again with seventy arrows.

sanskrit: bhūriśravās tu saṃkruddhaḥ pratodaṃ cicchide hareḥ arjunaṃ ca trisaptatyā bāṇānām ājaghāna ha
english: But Bhūriśravas, greatly enraged, cut off the goad of Hari and struck Arjuna with seventy-three arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatais tīkṣṇais tān arīñ śvetavāhanaḥ pratyaṣedhad drutaṃ kruddho mahāvāto ghanān iva
english: Then he of the white steeds, wrathful, swiftly checked those foes with hundreds of sharp arrows, as a mighty wind scatters the clouds.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dhvajān bahuvidhākārān bhrājamānān atiśriyā pārthānāṃ māmakānāṃ ca tān mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Of the banners of many shapes, gleaming with surpassing splendor, both of the sons of Pṛthā and of my own men — tell me of those, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dhvajān bahuvidhākārāñ śṛṇu teṣāṃ mahātmanām rūpato varṇataś caiva nāmataś ca nibodha me
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear of the banners of many shapes belonging to those high-souled ones; learn from me their forms, their colors, and their names.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu rathamuhyānāṃ ratheṣu vividhā dhvajāḥ pratyadṛśyanta rājendra jvalitā iva pāvakāḥ
english: Upon the chariots of those who rode therein, O lord of kings, divers banners were seen, blazing like fires.

sanskrit: kāñcanāḥ kāñcanāpīḍāḥ kāñcanasragalaṃkṛtāḥ kāñcanānīva śṛṅgāṇi kāñcanasya mahāgireḥ
english: Golden they were, with golden crests, adorned with golden wreaths, like the golden peaks of the great golden mountain.

sanskrit: te dhvajāḥ saṃvṛtās teṣāṃ patākābhiḥ samantataḥ nānāvarṇavirāgābhir vibabhuḥ sarvato vṛtāḥ
english: Those banners of theirs, wrapped about on every side with pennants of varied and brilliant hues, shone forth, encompassed all around.

sanskrit: patākāś ca tatas tās tu śvasanena samīritāḥ nṛtyamānāḥ vyadṛśyanta raṅgamadhye vilāsikāḥ
english: And those pennants, stirred by the wind, were seen dancing, like graceful courtesans amid the dancing-ground.

sanskrit: indrāyudhasavarṇābhāḥ patākā bharatarṣabha dodhūyamānā rathināṃ śobhayanti mahārathān
english: The pennants, glowing with the hues of Indra's bow, O bull of the Bhāratas, fluttering, lent beauty to those great car-warriors.

sanskrit: siṃhalāṅgūlam ugrāsyaṃ dhajaṃ vānaralakṣaṇam dhanaṃjayasya saṃgrāme pratyapaśyāma bhairavam
english: With its lion's tail and fierce mouth, the banner bearing the sign of the ape — Dhanaṃjaya's, terrible to behold — we beheld in the battle.

sanskrit: sa vānaravaro rājan patākābhir alaṃkṛtaḥ trāsayām āsa tat sainyaṃ dhvajo gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ
english: That foremost of apes, O king, adorned with pennants — the banner of the wielder of Gāṇḍīva — struck terror into that army.

sanskrit: tathaiva siṃhalāṅgūlaṃ droṇaputrasya bhārata dhvajāgraṃ samapaśyāma bālasūryasamaprabham
english: In like manner, O Bhārata, we beheld the lion's-tail crest atop the banner of Droṇa's son, radiant as the rising sun.

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ pavanoddhūtaṃ śakradhvajasamaprabham nandanaṃ kauravendrāṇāṃ drauṇer lakṣaṇam ucchritam
english: Golden, tossed by the wind, splendid as the banner of Śakra, gladdening the lords of the Kurus, the emblem of Droṇa's son was raised on high.

sanskrit: hastikakṣyā punar haimī babhūvādhirather dhvaje āhave khaṃ mahārāja dadṛśe pūrayann iva
english: And again, a golden elephant-girth was upon the banner of the son of Adhiratha, which in the battle, O great king, seemed to fill the very sky.

sanskrit: patākī kāñcanasragvī dhvajaḥ karṇasya saṃyuge nṛtyatīva rathopasthe śvasanena samīritaḥ
english: Decked with pennants and golden wreaths, the banner of Karṇa in the fight seemed to dance upon the chariot-platform, stirred by the wind.

sanskrit: ācāryasya ca pāṇḍūnāṃ brāhmaṇasya yaśasvinaḥ govṛṣo gautamasyāsīt kṛpasya supariṣkṛtaḥ
english: And the preceptor of the Pāṇḍus, the illustrious Brāhmaṇa Gautama, Kṛpa, bore a bull most finely wrought.

sanskrit: sa tena bhrājate rājan govṛṣeṇa mahārathaḥ tripuraghnaratho yadvad govṛṣeṇa virājate
english: With that bull, O king, the great car-warrior shone, even as the chariot of the destroyer of Tripura is resplendent with its bull.

sanskrit: mayūro vṛṣasenasya kāñcano maṇiratnavān vyāhariṣyann ivātiṣṭhat senāgram api śobhayan
english: Vṛṣasena's peacock, golden and set with gems and jewels, stood as if about to cry out, lending beauty even to the van of the host.

sanskrit: tena tasya ratho bhāti mayūreṇa mahātmanaḥ yathā skandasya rājendra mayūreṇa virājatā
english: With that peacock the chariot of that high-souled one shone, O lord of kings, even as Skanda's is resplendent with its glittering peacock.

sanskrit: madrarājasya śalyasya dhvajāgre 'gniśikhām iva sauvarṇīṃ pratipaśyāma sītām apratimāṃ śubhām
english: Atop the banner of Śalya, king of the Madras, we beheld a golden plough-furrow, peerless and fair, like a tongue of flame.

sanskrit: sā sītā bhrājate tasya ratham āsthāya māriṣa sarvabījavirūḍheva yathā sītā śriyā vṛtā
english: That furrow shone, set upon his chariot, O sire, as a furrow sprung up with every kind of seed, encompassed with splendor.

sanskrit: varāhaḥ sindhurājasya rājato 'bhivirājate dhvajāgre 'lohitārkābho hemajālapariṣkṛtaḥ
english: The boar of the king of the Sindhus, of silver, gleamed atop his banner, bright as the unreddened sun and wrought with a net of gold.

sanskrit: śuśubhe ketunā tena rājatena jayadrathaḥ yathā devāsure yuddhe purā pūṣā sma śobhate
english: With that silver standard Jayadratha shone forth, even as Pūṣan of old shone in the war of the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: saumadatteḥ punar yūpo yajñaśīlasya dhīmataḥ dhvajaḥ sūrya ivābhāti somaś cātra pradṛśyate
english: Again, the banner of the son of Somadatta — that wise one devoted to sacrifice — bore a sacrificial post that shone like the sun, and upon it the moon could be seen.

sanskrit: sa yūpaḥ kāñcano rājan saumadatter virājate rājasūye makhaśreṣṭhe yathā yūpaḥ samucchritaḥ
english: That golden sacrificial post of the son of Somadatta was resplendent, O king, like the post raised aloft at the Rājasūya, the foremost of sacrifices.

sanskrit: śalasya tu mahārāja rājato dvirado mahān ketuḥ kāñcanacitrāṅgair mayūrair upaśobhitaḥ
english: And Śala's standard, O great king, was a great silver elephant, adorned with peacocks whose limbs were variegated with gold.

sanskrit: sa ketuḥ śobhayām āsa sainyaṃ te bharatarṣabha yathā śveto mahānāgo devarājacamūṃ tathā
english: That standard lent beauty to your army, O bull of the Bhāratas, even as the great white elephant graces the host of the king of the gods.

sanskrit: nāgo maṇimayo rājño dhvajaḥ kanakasaṃvṛtaḥ kiṅkiṇīśatasaṃhrādo bhrājaṃś citre rathottame
english: The king's banner was an elephant fashioned of gems, sheathed in gold, ringing with a hundred little bells, shining upon his splendid and excellent chariot.

sanskrit: vyabhrājata bhṛśaṃ rājan putras tava viśāṃ pate dhvajena mahatā saṃkhye kurūṇām ṛṣabhas tadā
english: Your son shone forth exceedingly, O king, O lord of peoples, with that mighty banner in the battle — that bull among the Kurus.

sanskrit: navaite tava vāhinyām ucchritāḥ paramadhvajāḥ vyadīpayaṃs te pṛtanāṃ yugāntādityasaṃnibhāḥ
english: These nine supreme banners, raised aloft in your host, lit up the army, resembling the suns of the world's end.

sanskrit: daśamas tv arjunasyāsīd eka eva mahākapiḥ adīpyatārjuno yena himavān iva vahninā
english: But the tenth was Arjuna's — that one mighty ape alone — by which Arjuna blazed forth like the Himālaya wrapped in fire.

sanskrit: tataś citrāṇi śubhrāṇi sumahānti mahārathāḥ kārmukāṇy ādadus tūrṇam arjunārthe paraṃtapāḥ
english: Then those great car-warriors, scorchers of foes, swiftly took up their bows — variegated, bright, and very great — for the sake of opposing Arjuna.

sanskrit: tathaiva dhanur āyacchat pārthaḥ śatruvināśanaḥ gāṇḍīvaṃ divyakarmā tad rājan durmantrite tava
english: And so too Pārtha, the destroyer of foes, of divine deeds, drew his Gāṇḍīva, O king — all owing to your evil counsel.

sanskrit: tavāparādhād dhi narā nihatā bahudhā yudhi nānādigbhyaḥ samāhūtāḥ sahayāḥ sarathadvipāḥ
english: For through your fault many men, summoned from every quarter, were slain in the battle, together with their horses, their chariots, and their elephants.

sanskrit: teṣām āsīd vyatikṣepo garjatām itaretaram duryodhanamukhānāṃ ca pāṇḍūnām ṛṣabhasya ca
english: There arose a fierce exchange of blows among them, as they roared at one another — those led by Duryodhana and that bull among the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutaṃ paraṃ cakre kaunteyaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ yad eko bahubhiḥ sārdhaṃ samāgacchad abhītavat
english: There the son of Kuntī, with Kṛṣṇa for his charioteer, wrought a supreme marvel, in that, alone, he closed fearlessly with many.

sanskrit: aśobhata mahābāhur gāṇḍīvaṃ vikṣipan dhanuḥ jigīṣus tān naravyāghrāñ jighāṃsuś ca jayadratham
english: The mighty-armed one shone as he wielded the Gāṇḍīva bow, eager to vanquish those tigers among men and to slay Jayadratha.

sanskrit: tatrārjuno mahārāja śarair muktaiḥ sahasraśaḥ adṛśyān akarod yodhāṃs tāvakāñ śatrutāpanaḥ
english: There Arjuna, O great king, the tormentor of foes, with arrows loosed by the thousand, made your warriors invisible.

sanskrit: tatas te 'pi naravyāghrāḥ pārthaṃ sarve mahārathāḥ adṛśyaṃ samare cakruḥ sāyakaughaiḥ samantataḥ
english: Then those tigers among men too, all the great car-warriors, made Pārtha invisible in the battle with floods of arrows from every side.

sanskrit: saṃvṛte narasiṃhais taiḥ kurūṇām ṛṣabhe 'rjune mahān āsīt samuddhūtas tasya sainyasya nisvanaḥ
english: When Arjuna, that bull among the Kurus, was thus enveloped by those lions among men, a mighty uproar arose from that army.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca arjune saindhavaṃ prāpte bhāradvājena saṃvṛtāḥ pāñcālāḥ kurubhiḥ sārdhaṃ kim akurvata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When Arjuna had reached the ruler of the Sindhus, what did the Pāñcālas, hemmed in by the son of Bharadvāja together with the Kurus, do, Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca aparāhṇe mahārāja saṃgrāme lomaharṣaṇe pāñcālānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca droṇe dyūtam avartata
english: Saṃjaya said: In the afternoon, O great king, amid the hair-raising combat, a gambling-match was waged between the Pāñcālas and the Kurus over Droṇa.

sanskrit: pāñcālā hi jighāṃsanto droṇaṃ saṃhṛṣṭacetasaḥ abhyavarṣanta garjantaḥ śaravarṣāṇi māriṣa
english: For the Pāñcālas, eager to slay Droṇa, with hearts elated, poured down showers of arrows, roaring, O sire.

sanskrit: tataḥ sutumulas teṣāṃ saṃgrāmo 'vartatādbhutaḥ pāñcālānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca ghoro devāsuropamaḥ
english: Then a most tumultuous and wondrous battle was waged between them, between the Pāñcālas and the Kurus, terrible and like the war of the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: sarve droṇarathaṃ prāpya pāñcālāḥ paṇḍavaiḥ saha tad anīkaṃ bibhitsanto mahāstrāṇi vyadarśayan
english: All the Pāñcālas, together with the sons of Pāṇḍu, reaching the chariot of Droṇa and seeking to pierce that division, displayed their great weapons.

sanskrit: droṇasya rathaparyantaṃ rathino ratham āsthitāḥ kampayanto 'bhyavartanta vegam āsthāya madhyamam
english: The car-warriors, mounted upon their chariots, advanced right up to the chariot of Droṇa, making it tremble, pressing on at a moderate speed.
